title: Cheap South Florida Plans This Weekend
igCaption:
This weekend has a first-ever Indigenous film festival, museum shows, gallery stops, and Knaus Berry Farm reopening right after.
PAMM adult tickets are $18, and Knaus is setting a four-dozen cinnamon roll limit when it opens Tuesday.
Which one would you actually go to?

Sources: Miami New Times, Secret Miami

#SouthFlorida #WeekendGuide #ThingsToDo #FloridaEvents

scenes.text: South Florida has a cheap plan this weekend, with film, art, and a berry farm stop.

Start at Bill Cosford Cinema from Friday, October ninth through Monday, October twelfth. The first Miccosukee Indigenous Film Festival has twenty-two entries, all made under criteria tied to Indigenous writers, directors, producers, lead actors, or cultures.
scenes.caption: Start at Bill Cosford Cinema from Friday, Oct. 9 through Monday, Oct. 12. The first Miccosukee Indigenous Film Festival has 22 entries, all made under criteria tied to Indigenous writers, directors, producers, lead actors, or cultures.

scenes.text: For an art stop, Pérez Art Museum has two new shows that opened October first. Adult tickets cost eighteen dollars. Anina Major built a walkable environment with woven clay sculptures, and Zoë Buckman’s video work uses poetry around domestic violence.
scenes.caption: For an art stop, Pérez Art Museum has two new shows that opened Oct. 1. Adult tickets cost $18. Anina Major built a walkable environment with woven clay sculptures, and Zoë Buckman’s video work uses poetry around domestic violence.

scenes.text: Allapattah gives you two gallery stops close together. Voloshyn Gallery runs Maria Sulymenko’s watercolor and gouache show through October seventeenth at eight-oh-two Northwest Twenty-second Street. Spinello Projects runs Gabriel Pozzo’s solo show through October thirty-first on Northwest Seventh Avenue. If you hit both galleries, check NEAR to see who else was there.

scenes.text: Then save Tuesday for Knaus Berry Farm in the Redland. It reopens October thirteenth, two weeks early, and marks seventy years in business. Walk-up cinnamon roll orders now cap at four dozen per person, which still asks a lot of one car.

scenes.text: Which one would get you out of the house this weekend? That same feeling of passing people at a beach or market and never knowing who they were is exactly where NEAR comes in.
